## Functions or modules to implement

### 1. `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`: inline fallback `ensure_label_exists` (currently lines 914-938)
Change only the `else` branch that starts at `# Last-resort inline fallback if fetch fails.`:
- Keep the NOTE comment block (no `gh_retry`) byte-identical.
- Keep the `ensure_label_exists() {`, `local label_name="$1"` and `local repo="$2"` lines and the `case "${label_name}" in` line unchanged.
- Keep the `ai:ready-to-merge)` and `ai:closed)` arms byte-identical.
- Add three arms after `ai:closed)` and before `*)`. Each uses the same one-line shape `gh label create "${label_name}" --repo "${repo}" --color "<hex>" --description "<text>" 2>/dev/null || true`, then `;;` at 10 spaces of indentation, matching the existing arms:
  - `ai:clarification)` with `--color "f9d0c4" --description "AI clarification required before planning"`
  - `ai:orchestrator-managed)` with `--color "bfdadc" --description "Issue is managed by the AI orchestrator"`
  - `ai:workflow-heal)` with `--color "d876e3" --description "Issue auto-filed from an escalated workflow failure by workflow failure heal"`
- Values are copied from `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` lines 4-7, 164-167 and 220-223.
- In the `*)` arm, before the unchanged generic `gh label create ... --color "1d76db" --description "AI workflow label" 2>/dev/null || true` line:
  - Add a short assumption comment: the analysis doc suggested refusing unknown labels. We keep creating them, because skipping creation could make a later `--add-label` / `--label` fail and break the judge flow. `test_review_rb_judge_fallback_label_metadata_matches_label_contract` keeps this arm unreachable from current literal call sites.
  - Add `echo "::warning::ensure_label_exists fallback: label '${label_name}' has no contract metadata in the inline fallback; creating it with generic metadata." >&2`.
- The warning goes to stderr so no caller that might capture stdout gets polluted. Today no call site captures it: none of the `ensure_label_exists` lines is inside `$(...)` or a pipe. The label name comes from the script's own literals, and a `::warning::` annotation is valid on either stream.
- Leave the helper-loading order (local source, then verified 40-hex `SCRIPT_REF` fetch, then inline fallback) untouched. Use 2-space-step indentation, matching the block.

### 2. `tests/test_ai_label_precreation_contract.py`: new test `test_review_rb_judge_fallback_label_metadata_matches_label_contract`
Follow the style of `test_review_autofix_label_metadata_matches_label_contract`: tabs, a `problems` list, and one final `assert not problems, "\n".join(problems)`.
- Add module constants with unique names. Checked: none of these clash with the existing `LABEL_CONTRACT_PATH`, `PINNED_REVIEW_AUTOFIX_LABELS`, `GENERIC_LABEL_FALLBACK` or `_*_RE` names.
  - `REVIEW_RB_JUDGE_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/review_rb_judge.sh"`
  - `_RB_FALLBACK_DEF_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*ensure_label_exists\(\)\s*\{\s*$")`
  - `_RB_FALLBACK_ESAC_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*esac\s*$")`
  - `_RB_DEFAULT_ARM_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\*\)\s*$")`
- New helper `_review_rb_judge_fallback_arms(text) -> dict[str, list[str]]`:
  - Find the single line matching `_RB_FALLBACK_DEF_RE`. Assert exactly one exists, otherwise extraction is broken.
  - Walk forward to the first `_RB_FALLBACK_ESAC_RE` line.
  - Split into arms keyed by `_CASE_ARM_RE` (reuse it) and `"*"` for `_RB_DEFAULT_ARM_RE`, collecting each arm's body lines up to `;;`.
- New helper `_all_label_contract_metadata() -> dict[str, tuple[str, str]]`. It reads every entry of `contract["labels"]` and leaves the existing PINNED-only `_load_label_contract_metadata` alone.
- Test body:
  1. `literals = sorted(set(_ENSURE_LITERAL_RE.findall(text)))` (reuse the existing regex). Assert that the five known labels `ai:ready-to-merge`, `ai:closed`, `ai:clarification`, `ai:orchestrator-managed` and `ai:workflow-heal` are a subset of it. This guards against extraction silently returning nothing.
  2. For each literal: there must be an explicit arm (not just `*`), and the label must exist in the contract.
  3. For each explicit `ai:*` arm: exactly one `_FORM_B_RE` match (reuse the regex), whose `(color, description)` equals the contract entry. The arm line must also contain `gh label create "${label_name}"` and end with `2>/dev/null || true`, and the arm must not contain `gh_retry`. That keeps the NOTE invariant.
  4. The `*` arm must exist, contain `::warning::` and still contain the `GENERIC_LABEL_FALLBACK` color and description, so unknown labels are still created.
  5. Error messages name `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`, the label and expected vs actual values, in the style of the existing test.
- Add the new test call to the `if __name__ == "__main__":` block before `print("PASS")`.

Unknown labels are still created but now emit a `::warning::`.

## Data structures affected
- None at runtime. The bash `case` table in the fallback gains three entries. The test adds read-only parsing of `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json`, which is not modified.

## API or interface changes
- None. The function name `ensure_label_exists` and its `label repo` signature are unchanged. There are no new env vars, no renamed identifiers and no workflow YAML edits. The only new observable is one `::warning::` line on the unreachable `*)` path.

## Decisions

### D1 — Keep creating unknown labels in the `*)` arm, with a warning
- Chosen: emit `::warning::` and still create the label with the generic metadata.
- Alternatives considered: refuse unknown labels (return without creating), as the analysis doc suggested; or fail the step.
- Why: the later `gh issue edit --add-label` / `gh issue create --label` calls would fail on a missing label and break the judge flow. That conflicts with §6 Correctness and §2 "preserve existing behavior". The new test keeps the arm unreachable from literal call sites.

### D2 — Warning goes to stderr
- Chosen: `echo "::warning::..." >&2`.
- Alternatives considered: stdout, as at `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:60`.
- Why: GitHub parses workflow commands on both streams. Stderr cannot corrupt a future `$(ensure_label_exists ...)` capture, and the script already uses `>&2` for warnings (line 207).

### D3 — Static source-parsing test, no shell execution
- Chosen: parse the fallback `case` block and the literal call sites from the script text, and compare against the JSON contract.
- Alternatives considered: run the extracted function under bash with a stub `gh`.
- Why: the issue asks for a static contract in the style of `test_review_autofix_label_metadata_matches_label_contract`. Static parsing covers both acceptance criteria (missing arm, metadata drift) deterministically and needs no subprocess fixtures.

### D4 — New all-labels contract loader instead of changing `_load_label_contract_metadata`
- Chosen: add `_all_label_contract_metadata()`.
- Alternatives considered: widen `PINNED_REVIEW_AUTOFIX_LABELS`.
- Why: widening it would change what the existing review_autofix test asserts (it requires a metadata site for every pinned label). §9/§10 forbid repurposing existing identifiers.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: unchanged. The fallback only runs after both the local source and the verified 40-hex `SCRIPT_REF` fetch fail. The fetch gate and `wf_source` are not touched, so there is no new remote-code path.
- Authorization: there is no new endpoint or surface. `gh label create` runs with the job's existing token and label-write scope.
- External input: label names at the call sites are script literals. The warning interpolates `${label_name}` inside double quotes, so there is no command injection. An unknown name from a future dynamic call site would only print in the annotation, and labels contain no secrets.
- Abuse cases: an attacker cannot force the fallback path and get different metadata beyond what the contract defines, because fallback metadata now equals the contract. Spoofing a `::warning::` annotation
